units.rhetorical_move: the work is opened by what motivated it
units.function: a motive stands in for the problem

original_instantiations: the reason for the work comes before the work itself
the motive is accuracy

units.source_excerpt: Motivated to measure a country's stability quantitatively and more accurately, our team builds a framework.
units.reusable_pattern: open with the motive rather than the task
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the subject wording

units.rhetorical_move: a system is said to describe and also to predict
units.function: one tool is given two jobs

original_instantiations: the same system is said to show the present and the destination
the second job is the forecast

units.source_excerpt: This system not only describes the current fragility, but also it predicts the equilibrium states the country would approach.
units.reusable_pattern: give one system a present job and a future job
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the system wording

units.rhetorical_move: a plot is proposed that depicts the tipping points
units.function: a figure is announced as the result

original_instantiations: the picture is said to carry the boundaries between the states
the states are named after the claim

units.source_excerpt: We propose a bifurcation plot that depicts the tipping points between three states of a country.
units.reusable_pattern: announce a plot as the carrier of the boundaries
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the state names

units.rhetorical_move: a finding is reached after calibrating and comparing
units.function: the method is named before the result

original_instantiations: the steps come first and the discovery follows
the discovery is a role for one factor

units.source_excerpt: After calibrating parameters and comparing factors, we find that climate conditions play a significant role.
units.reusable_pattern: lead a finding with the steps that produced it
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the country name

units.rhetorical_move: a list of effects is given and then the doubt
units.function: the consensus is undercut at once

original_instantiations: the accepted effects are named and the disagreement follows in the same breath
the doubt is the point

units.source_excerpt: Climate change includes droughts, shrinking glaciers and sea level rise. Despite a consensus, denial and doubts still exist.
units.reusable_pattern: set a consensus against the doubt that survives it
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the subject wording

units.rhetorical_move: the paper is mapped by section numbers
units.function: a roadmap uses the section numbers

original_instantiations: each later section is named by its number and its job
the reader is told where to look

units.source_excerpt: In one section we select countries to do case studies. In the next, we examine the effects of intervention and estimate the cost.
units.reusable_pattern: map the paper by its section numbers
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the section numbers

units.rhetorical_move: a unit is chosen because it is more efficient
units.function: a measurement choice is justified by convenience

original_instantiations: dollars are picked since they make the effects easier to compare
the convenience is the whole reason

units.source_excerpt: We measure the impacts in the unit of dollars because we think it is more efficient to quantify the extent of the effects.
units.reusable_pattern: justify a unit by how easy it makes the comparison
reusable_elements: because we think it is more efficient
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the unit

units.rhetorical_move: a definition is made for consistency and data collection
units.function: a narrowing is given two practical reasons

original_instantiations: the word is pinned to one meaning so the data stays comparable
both reasons are practical

units.source_excerpt: We define the state as a country for consistency and data collection purpose.
units.reusable_pattern: narrow a term for consistency and for the data
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the term

units.rhetorical_move: trustworthiness is inferred from reliable sources
units.function: a leap is made from source to accuracy

original_instantiations: the sources are called reliable, so the numbers are called accurate
the leap is marked by thus

units.source_excerpt: We assume all data are trustworthy since all sources are reliable. Thus, we are confident that our metrics reflect the accurate condition.
units.reusable_pattern: treat reliable sources as accurate data
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the source names

units.rhetorical_move: three states are defined before the model
units.function: the labels come first

original_instantiations: the categories are fixed ahead of any equation
the order is the point

units.source_excerpt: Before devising our model, we first define three possible states of a country.
units.reusable_pattern: define the categories before building the model
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the state names

units.rhetorical_move: a state is said to recover and return to equilibrium
units.function: stability is defined by the return

original_instantiations: the test of the state is whether it comes back after a shock
the return is the definition

units.source_excerpt: Even if there is a crisis, such a country can quickly recover and return to its equilibrium state.
units.reusable_pattern: define a state by how fast it returns
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the state name

units.rhetorical_move: a small turbulence is said to bring large impacts
units.function: fragility is defined by amplification

original_instantiations: the state is the one where a small push has a big result
the amplification is the whole definition

units.source_excerpt: As a result, any small turbulence could bring large impacts on all factors.
units.reusable_pattern: define fragility as small causes with large effects
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the factor names

units.rhetorical_move: money is said to be not the sole predictor
units.function: a chosen measure is immediately limited

original_instantiations: the unit just chosen is said to be insufficient on its own
the other factors follow

units.source_excerpt: However, we believe that money is not the sole predictor of the fragility of a country.
units.reusable_pattern: limit the measure just adopted
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the measure

units.rhetorical_move: the growth rate is said to be independent of time
units.function: a property is named and then translated

original_instantiations: the technical word is given and then said in plain words

units.source_excerpt: We realize that the derivative is an autonomous function, that is, the growth rate is not dependent on time.
units.reusable_pattern: gloss a technical term with that is
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the term

units.rhetorical_move: a function is borrowed from an outbreak model
units.function: the source of the equation is named

original_instantiations: the shape is credited to an earlier paper
the credit comes before the use

units.source_excerpt: Inspired by the outbreak system of an earlier paper, we obtain the functions above.
units.reusable_pattern: credit the shape of an equation to its source
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the citation

units.rhetorical_move: a loss is said to show signs and then turn on quickly
units.function: a threshold is narrated

original_instantiations: the effect is small at first and sudden once a level is passed
the level is the whole point

units.source_excerpt: When the market is small the impact would only show signs. When it exceeds a critical level, the impact would turn on quickly.
units.reusable_pattern: narrate a threshold as a switch
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the variable names

units.rhetorical_move: the metrics are called similar but more concise
units.function: a borrowed list is trimmed

original_instantiations: the published list is the start and the overlaps are the reason for cutting
the cut is the contribution

units.source_excerpt: Our metrics are similar to the published indicators. But our metrics will be more concise because we find overlapping variables.
units.reusable_pattern: trim a borrowed list for its overlaps
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the index name

units.rhetorical_move: a dataset is rejected because it is not public
units.function: a substitution is blamed on access

original_instantiations: the preferred source is closed, so a second one is used
the reason is stated

units.source_excerpt: However, the data is not publicly available. So we use the results provided by another source.
units.reusable_pattern: replace a closed dataset and say so
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the source names

units.rhetorical_move: a factor is dropped because it does not apply to every country
units.function: a variable is excluded for scope

original_instantiations: the factor is called important and then set aside as not universal
a related factor stands in

units.source_excerpt: Although the factor is a major component, it is not a typical question for all countries. So we consider a related one instead.
units.reusable_pattern: drop a factor that does not apply everywhere
reusable_elements: it is not a typical question
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the factor name

units.rhetorical_move: a widely used measure is rejected for a narrower one
units.function: the popular choice is declined

original_instantiations: the common measure is set aside because it counts the wrong thing
the wanted measure is named

units.source_excerpt: Although the common measure is more widely used, we think the other works better because we want the well-being of a country.
units.reusable_pattern: reject the popular measure for the one that fits
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the measure names

units.rhetorical_move: a threshold is preferred because the lower one means starving
units.function: a data choice is argued from daily life

original_instantiations: the lower line is said to be unsurvivable and the higher one adequate
the argument is ordinary experience

units.source_excerpt: We think the higher daily amount reflects a normal level of spending better, since the lower one makes it difficult to live.
units.reusable_pattern: choose a data threshold by what a person can live on
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the amounts

units.rhetorical_move: two terms are introduced and then defined
units.function: the vocabulary is fixed before the analysis

original_instantiations: the two words are named and each is given its meaning
the meanings are plain

units.source_excerpt: Hence, we introduce two terms. One describes a fixed point. The other describes the watersheds between stages.
units.reusable_pattern: introduce terms and define them immediately
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the term names

units.rhetorical_move: a root is called unstable on intuition
units.function: a stability claim rests on a hunch

original_instantiations: the judgement is offered as obvious rather than proven
the reason follows the hunch

units.source_excerpt: Intuitively, the zero root is always unstable, because near it the supply would grow.
units.reusable_pattern: mark a stability claim as intuitive
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the variable

units.rhetorical_move: the analysis is said to be easier graphically
units.function: a picture replaces the algebra

original_instantiations: the intersections are said to be simpler than solving
the figure does the work

units.source_excerpt: It is easier to analyze the equation graphically, in that we could simply find the intersections.
units.reusable_pattern: prefer a figure to a solution
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the equation

units.rhetorical_move: a curve with one fixed point is read as a fragile country
units.function: a shape is given a label

original_instantiations: the single low root is said to behave like one kind of country
the reading is offered as a thought

units.source_excerpt: So we think this solution curve exhibits similar behavior as a fragile country.
units.reusable_pattern: read a curve shape as a kind of country
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the state name

units.rhetorical_move: a result is said to be largely explained by two reasons
units.function: a claim is split into numbered grounds

original_instantiations: the explanation is announced as two and then given
the count comes first

units.source_excerpt: This can be largely explained by two reasons. First, the solution is always attracted to the equilibrium. Second, the rate of recovering is greater.
units.reusable_pattern: announce two reasons and then give them
reusable_elements: can be largely explained by two reasons
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the subject wording

units.rhetorical_move: a factor is removed to see the change
units.function: a test is described as an omission

original_instantiations: one input is dropped and the picture is redrawn
the purpose is the comparison

units.source_excerpt: To determine how the change increased the fragility, we omitted that factor from our variables.
units.reusable_pattern: test a factor by removing it
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the factor name

units.rhetorical_move: the shift is said to correspond to the research
units.function: a picture and a source are said to agree

original_instantiations: the movement on the plot is matched to what was read
the agreement is the claim

units.source_excerpt: This corresponds to our research that the condition played a significant role.
units.reusable_pattern: match a plot shift to the reading
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the country name

units.rhetorical_move: a replacement with the global average is used as the test
units.function: the counterfactual is a normal year

original_instantiations: the extreme values are swapped for the ordinary ones
the ordinary case is the comparison

units.source_excerpt: By replacing these factors with the global average, we can see an increase in the parameter.
units.reusable_pattern: build a counterfactual from the global average
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the factor names

units.rhetorical_move: a graph is said to confirm the expectation
units.function: agreement is taken as validation

original_instantiations: the picture matching the prior belief is offered as proof
the belief came from the reading

units.source_excerpt: This finding confirms our expectation based on our research and suggests the robustness of our framework.
units.reusable_pattern: treat agreement with expectation as validation
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the country name

units.rhetorical_move: a cost is projected as more than a round number
units.function: a forecast is given as a floor

original_instantiations: the spending is said to exceed a stated amount by a stated year
the floor is the whole result

units.source_excerpt: Based on our model, we project that the total cost would be more than the stated sum by the stated year.
units.reusable_pattern: report a cost as a lower bound
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the figures

units.rhetorical_move: a small unit is said to be easy and a large one difficult
units.function: the two scales are split

original_instantiations: the same model is said to transfer downward but not upward
the difficulty is definitional

units.source_excerpt: Our model can be used for small units. However, it may be difficult for larger ones because we have to change our definition of the data.
units.reusable_pattern: split the scaling claim by direction
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the unit names

units.rhetorical_move: a mean is proposed with population as the weight
units.function: a fix is sketched

original_instantiations: the larger unit is handled by weighting its members
the weight is named

units.source_excerpt: We may use the size of each member as a weight to calculate a mean for the whole.
units.reusable_pattern: reduce a large unit to a weighted mean
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the unit name

units.rhetorical_move: flexibility is traced to independent parameters
units.function: a strength is given its cause

original_instantiations: the parameters do not depend on each other, so one can be swapped
the independence is the strength

units.source_excerpt: One strength is its flexibility. All the parameters are relatively independent. Hence, it is easy to change one.
units.reusable_pattern: derive flexibility from independent parameters
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the parameter names

units.rhetorical_move: a fit to a published index is called accuracy
units.function: agreement is promoted to correctness

original_instantiations: matching the published ranking is offered as proof of accuracy
the match is the only evidence

units.source_excerpt: Another strength is that it fits the result from the published index, which shows the accuracy of our model.
units.reusable_pattern: call a fit to a published index accuracy
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the index name

units.rhetorical_move: the weights are said to need revision
units.function: a limit is stated as future work

original_instantiations: the current weights are admitted to be provisional
the fix is a revision

units.source_excerpt: One limitation is that the weight of each parameter may be revised to make the model more accurate.
units.reusable_pattern: state a limitation as a needed revision
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the parameter names

units.rhetorical_move: interactions between countries are said to be left out
units.function: an omission is owned

original_instantiations: the model treats each country alone and the paper says so
the missing link is named

units.source_excerpt: We did not account for the interaction between countries, which may play an important role.
units.reusable_pattern: own a missing interaction
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the subject wording

units.rhetorical_move: the framework is said to have been developed
units.function: the close restates the build

original_instantiations: the whole construction is named once more
the factors are listed again

units.source_excerpt: In our paper, we have developed a framework that measures the fragility of a state, taking account of the factors.
units.reusable_pattern: close by restating what was built
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the factor names

units.rhetorical_move: the results are said to follow a published ranking
units.function: the validation is repeated at the end

original_instantiations: the three cases are said to land where the published list puts them
the agreement is the last word

units.source_excerpt: Our results follow the latest ranking, where the three countries are considered fragile, vulnerable and stable respectively.
units.reusable_pattern: end on the agreement with a published ranking
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the country names

units.rhetorical_move: each source sits on its own line with the year in parentheses
units.function: the list mixes reports, journal articles and data pages

original_instantiations: a report, an article and a data page each take a line
the kinds of source stay apart by entry

units.source_excerpt: Ludwig, D., Jones, D. D., and Holling, C. S. (1978). Qualitative analysis of insect outbreak systems.
units.reusable_pattern: give each source its own author-year line
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the list as prose
